The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 19.11.2023.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 19.11.2023 at about 7.40 p.m., petitioner was riding a Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 05-H-7550 from Vignan Nagar towards Annsandra Palya by wearing headguard slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing on moving vehicles, when he reached near Shall Petrol Bunk, at that time the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-01- NA-2834 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed from Jain Heights Apartments and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to forced impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was treated as in-patient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/-
towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 65 years, the petitioner was doing real estate business and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do job and hence lost his earnings.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, hence placed exparte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
This respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liabilities if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 134(c), 158(6) and 170 of M. V. Act.

This respondent specifically submits that car bearing reg. No. KA-01-NA-2834 was not involved in the accident and jurisdictional police have filed the false charge sheet against the insured vehicle by colluding with the petitioner without conducting the proper investigation.

Further, this respondent submits that, at the time of alleged accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding Driving License to drive the vehicle, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.11.2023 at about 7.40 p.m., accident took place near Shall Petrol Bunk, Basavanagara main road, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-01-NA-2834 as a result the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14, examined one Vedavathi.
N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.15 and 16, examined Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.17 and 18 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
8.
ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.

He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.

Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.13 is the Notarized copy of Driving License and Ex.P.14 are the Medical Bills.

10. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 19.11.2023 at about 7.40 p.m., petitioner was riding a Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-H-7550 from Vignan Nagar towards Annsandra Palya by wearing headguard slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing on moving vehicles, when he reached near Shall Petrol Bunk, at that time the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-01-NA-2834 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed from Jain Heights Apartments and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to forced impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was treated as in-patient.
Accordingly, the Airport Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.261/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg. No. KA-01-NA-2834.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Airport Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 261/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of the driver of offending Car.

The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending Car U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.

Further in this case, contesting respondent has taken contention that, the Car bearing Reg. No.
KA-01-NA-2834 was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle and the said alleged accident is caused due to the sole negligence of petitioner.

Further during cross- examination of petitioner i.e., PW.1, learned counsel for respondent No.2 suggested that, alleged accident is not caused due to the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-01- NA-2834 and petitioner himself rode his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, as such accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner only, but witness denied the said suggestion.
Moreover, in order to prove his contention contesting respondent failed to adduce evidence before this court.
Hence, as per the decision reported in (1999) 3 SCC 573 between Vidhyadhar vs Manikrao & Anr.
presumption
would arise that the case set up by the respondent is not correct.

16. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: 17. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-01-NA-2834.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING:
In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he treated as an inpatient from 19.11.2023 to 22.11.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Manipal Hospital, Bangalore for 03 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which disclose that petitioner sustained fracture of both bones (radius & ulna) of the left forearm and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 16 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.2,68,894/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,68,894/-
towards medical expenses.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summaries issued by Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 19.11.2023 to 22.11.2023 i.e. for total 03 days.

sentences.text: Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was doing Real Estate Business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/-
per month.
But respondent No.2 disputed the income of petitioner, but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner to show how much income he was getting from his work.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/-
as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2023.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.

Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/-
under this head.
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. S. Ramachandra in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 who has opined that, total disability of whole body disability at 12.32.%.
Admittedly, the PW.3 is not a treated doctor.

Same was admitted by the PW.3 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.3 reads as follows :
"It is true to say that, I have not personally treated the petitioner."

He was sworn that, petitioner sustained left forearm both bones (radius and ulna) fracture and further depose that, petitioner has got 12.32% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 6% of disability to the petitioner.
PW.2 is only Senior Technician, who has only produced the medical documents and his evidence is formal in nature.
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.12 is the Aadhar card of the petitioner, wherein year of birth is mentioned as 1954 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 69 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '5'.

sentences.text: Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.57,600/-.

24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 19.11.2023 to 22.11.2023 i.e. for total 03 days.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 69 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 2,68,894/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 32,000/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning, Rs. 57,600/-
Disability 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
loss of happiness.
Total Rs. 4,58,494/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,58,494/- under various heads.
26. LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-01-NA-2834 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending Car.
The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.4,58,494/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, entire amount shall be released in his name on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

But respondent No.2 disputed the income of petitioner, but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner to show how much income he was getting from his work.

28. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.4,58,494/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, entire amount shall be released in his name on proper identification.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
